analysis:
The 31 March 2026 target was repeated by Shah through 2024 and 2025 (Chhattisgarh visits in December 2024, June 2025 and October 2025 per press reports) and linked to a 24 August 2024 meeting of state police chiefs, per Shah's own account.

On 30 March 2026 Shah told the Lok Sabha that 706 Maoists were killed, 2,218 arrested and 4,839 surrendered over three years, and said India had become Naxal-free while a formal announcement was pending. On 19 May 2026 he said at a Jagdalpur press conference that Naxalism had been completely eradicated before the deadline.

Official LWE data show a large decline: deaths from 1,005 in 2010 to 130 in 2024 (Dataful compiling MHA data). Reports on the number of districts still classed as affected vary: ORF cites two, another source cites six 'most affected' in 2025, and one summary cites zero as of April 2026. ORF notes the statistics are government-supplied and that a Maoist leader was reportedly still at large.

Because the central claim of complete eradication is a government self-assessment with no independent audit available to this review, and the sources conflict on residual districts, the entry is marked in-progress rather than true.
